content: Charity Hospital is one of two teaching hospitals that are part of the Medical Center of Louisiana at New Orleans (MCLNO). It is one of several public hospitals in Louisiana administered by the Louisiana State University (LSU) System. Both Charity Hospital and the nearby University Hospital are teaching hospitals affiliated with the LSU Health Sciences Center in New Orleans (LSUHSC-NO). Charity Hospital is located in the New Orleans Hospital District, on the opposite side of Interstate 10 from the LSU Health Sciences Center. Its address is 1532 Tulane Avenue, New Orleans, Louisiana, 70112-1352. Charity Hospital was founded on May 10, 1736, through a grant from Jean Louis, a French sailor and shipbuilder who passed away in New Orleans the year prior. His will directed that his estate be used to fund a hospital for the indigent in the colony of New Orleans. For over 250 years, the hospital has served the poor in the city. Originally named the Hospital of Saint John or L’Hôpital des Pauvres de la Charité (French for Hospital for the Poor), the first Charity Hospital was located at the intersection of Chartres Street and Bienville Street in what is now the French Quarter. It was established 18 years after the city of New Orleans was founded by France in 1718. Charity Hospital is the second-oldest continuously operating public hospital in the United States, with only Bellevue Hospital in New York City being older, founded just a month earlier on March 31, 1736. The original facility of Charity Hospital quickly became inadequate, leading to the construction of a second hospital at the edge of the colony on Basin Street in 1743. A third hospital was built nearby in 1785. After New Orleans was ceded to Spain in 1763, this hospital was renamed San Carlos Hospital in honor of King Charles III of Spain. However, a fire destroyed the hospital in 1809. In the absence of a permanent building, temporary facilities were established at the Cabildo for a month, then at the Jourdan residence in the Faubourg Marigny for six months, and finally at the dilapidated De La Vergne plantation for five years. A fourth hospital was constructed at the edge of the city on Canal Street, where the Fairmont Hotel now stands, and was completed in 1815. However, this facility was widely criticized for being inadequate and underfunded. In 1832, a fifth hospital was built within the area bounded by Girod, Gravier, St. Mary, and Common Streets in the Faubourg St. Marie. This hospital came under the administration of the Sisters of Charity, who managed it for the next century. Under their care, Charity Hospital became a renowned institution for healing in New Orleans. By the 20th century, the city’s rapid expansion and increasing demand for indigent medical services once again exceeded the hospital’s capacity. In 1939, a sixth hospital was constructed on Tulane Avenue. With 2,680 beds, it was the second-largest hospital in the United States at the time. The LSU Health Sciences Center in New Orleans (LSUHSC-NO) was built adjacent to Charity Hospital in 1931. Charity Hospital served one of the largest populations of uninsured citizens in the country and was home to the second-ranked Level I Trauma Center in the nation, with the top-ranked center being Cook County Hospital in Chicago, Illinois. In 1970, the Louisiana Department of Health and Human Resources (DHH) assumed control of Charity Hospital. The hospital was later transferred to the Louisiana Health Care Authority (LHCA) in 1991 and then to the LSU System in 1997. During Hurricane Katrina, Charity Hospital sustained severe flood damage, similar to its sister institution, University Hospital. The evacuation of patients from the flooded hospital garnered national attention. Following the storm, a temporary clinic named the Spirit of Charity was established at the Convention Center. This clinic was later relocated to the New Orleans Centre building adjacent to the Superdome. By February 2007, a renovated University Hospital had taken over the emergency care responsibilities that Charity Hospital had previously provided. The future of Charity Hospital remains uncertain. LSUHSC has announced plans to construct a new modern facility nearby, named the Medical Center of Louisiana at New Orleans (MCLNO). If funding for this new hospital is approved by the Louisiana State Legislature, it would consolidate the functions of both Charity Hospital and University Hospital.
